correctness.rationale: All rows of the constructed matrix are nonzero and have constant leverage by an explicit orthonormal left factor. Group-count multinomial distribution gives an exact diagonal sampled product; all weak Gram modes contribute at most (d-1)/d² in relative operator norm. Binomial integer bands classify the strong mode exactly, endpoint-safe Poisson convergence follows from the binomial generating function, and the norm-based one-draw success event is computed by direct rescaling. Proof checks all integer budgets 1<=r<d² and the stipulated epsilon range; 9,371 exact-arithmetic checks verify representative instances, not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: A natural numerical task—relative operator-norm Gram approximation—has an exact sample-budget feasibility classification under the precise published joint-leverage sketch. The all-nonzero-row flat-leverage family has stable rank tending to one yet shows strict increases in sample budget can force guaranteed failure, followed by renewed success. A one-sample, near-certain alternative for the same target provides a concrete sampling-design benchmark without claiming universal optimality or contradicting subspace embeddings.
